items.title: Reduce service account token exposure
items.rationale: Mounted service account tokens expand blast radius when a pod is compromised and should be disabled unless the workload truly needs Kubernetes API access.
actions: Set automountServiceAccountToken: false for workloads that do not need the API.
Use a dedicated least-privilege service account when API access is required.
Keep token mounts read-only and review RBAC bindings.

items.title: Mount the root filesystem read-only
items.rationale: Writable root filesystems make persistence and tampering easier after compromise.
actions: Move writable paths to explicit emptyDir or persistent volumes.
Validate startup scripts and temp directories still work after the change.
items.snippet:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: REPLACE_ME
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: target-kata,role=target
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      containers:
      - name: REPLACE_ME
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
          runAsUser: 10001
          runAsGroup: 10001
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
          capabilities:
            drop: ["ALL"]
          seccompProfile:
            type: RuntimeDefault
items.risk_note: Enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem can break workloads that write under /tmp, /var, /etc, or application paths.
items.manual_recommendation: Identify writable paths and move them to explicit volumes or emptyDir mounts first.

templates.kyverno_policy:
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: sandbox-restricted
spec:
  validationFailureAction: Audit
  rules:
  - name: require-restricted-security-context
    match:
      resources:
        kinds:
        - Pod
    validate:
      message: Enforce restricted securityContext for sandbox workloads.
      pattern:
        spec:
          containers:
          - securityContext:
              allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
              readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
              seccompProfile:
                type: RuntimeDefault
templates.gatekeeper_template:
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRequiredSandboxSecurity
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8srequiredsandboxsecurity
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Pod"
        not input.review.object.spec.containers[_].securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem
        msg := "Sandbox pods must set readOnlyRootFilesystem=true"
      }

ai_advisor.executive_summary: Three security issues found for Deployment target-kata (namespace sandbox-kata): exposed service account token, writable root filesystem, and setuid/setgid binaries in the image. Risk band: high (total 14).
ai_advisor.remediation_overview: All fixes require operator review. Two fixes (serviceAccount automount and readOnlyRootFilesystem) can be patched but may break the workload; image rebuild needed to remove setuid/setgid binaries. Validate compatibility before applying.

prioritized_groups.title: Service account token exposure
prioritized_groups.rationale: High severity and high blast radius; tokens enable Kubernetes API access from the pod.

prioritized_groups.title: Writable root filesystem
prioritized_groups.rationale: High severity: writable root increases attack surface; enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem hardens container but can break writes.

prioritized_groups.title: Setuid/setgid binaries in image
prioritized_groups.rationale: Medium severity; requires image rebuild and validation of admin tooling.

item_advice.explanation: Pod automounts a service account token, allowing in-cluster API access which increases credential exposure.
item_advice.operator_impact: Disabling automount breaks any in-pod code that calls the Kubernetes API or uses the token.
item_advice.validation_advice: Search code/config for Kubernetes client use, exec into a staging pod to confirm behavior, and test after disabling automount.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Mitigates highest-risk access vector quickly; requires operator confirmation before change.

item_advice.explanation: Container root filesystem is writable, enabling attackers to modify binaries or persistence on compromise.
item_advice.operator_impact: Setting readOnlyRootFilesystem may break apps that write to /tmp, /var, /etc, or application directories; move writable paths to volumes first.
item_advice.validation_advice: Inspect container for writable paths, run workload in staging with readOnlyRootFilesystem=true, and ensure logs/state are redirected to declared volumes.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Hardens container filesystem; test before applying to avoid downtime.

item_advice.explanation: Image contains setuid/setgid binaries which can be used for privilege escalation if exploited.
item_advice.operator_impact: Remediation requires rebuilding images and may remove admin utilities relied on by operators or processes.
item_advice.validation_advice: List setuid/setgid files in the image, rebuild on minimal base removing unnecessary helpers, and test functionality in staging.
item_advice.ordering_reason: Lower blast radius but requires image workflow changes; do after immediate mitigations.

ai_advisor.guided_operator_message: Review service-account and filesystem changes in staging first; only apply image rebuilds after validating functionality.
warnings: Do not disable automount if the pod legitimately uses the Kubernetes API.
Enabling readOnlyRootFilesystem can cause application failures if writable paths aren’t remapped.
Removing setuid/setgid binaries may remove required admin tooling—validate in CI/staging.
next_steps: Confirm whether pod uses Kubernetes API and, if not, disable automountServiceAccountToken on the pod spec.
Identify writable paths; create explicit volumes (emptyDir) for runtime writes and then enable readOnlyRootFilesystem.
